interactions.title: The hunter’s pursuit and the attack’s end
lines: DM: Okay. So his first memory is the searing pain of new sunlight. Does not understand the whispers that echo in his head, but they awaken something in him. The pain of the sunlight fades to a dull background ache, easily ignored. The walls around him—a courtyard, he thinks, although words are hard to remember now—fade to a pale shadow, and suddenly he can see, feel in the far distance a bright light. His quarry. You must get there and bring it back, whatever it is. The light of this quarry is so distant across mountains and deserts, but it does not matter. As darkness falls, the bright light of his quarry grows stronger without the sun to distract him.

DM: He gives a call, a twisted shout, and feels the massive wing beats of an approaching gloom stalker, a Wyvern-like creature made of shadows. He leaps into the sky, soaring, and sees behind him another gloom stalker carrying another hunter like him. Like him. Good! He will not be alone. Then the first nights he flies south. The movement of his quarry tracking south as well, far to the east. They're moving much faster than he is, but he does not care, for eventually they must stop long enough for him to catch up. Then a pause as he gains ground, but it is short-lived, and they begin moving again. A stroke of fortune: they turned west, heading for him. Will only be a few days now.

DM: Does not care how they were able to travel so quickly. Now it helps him as his quarry rapidly approaches. The light grows bright, intense, and the taste of victory taunts him. It reminds him of something, some forgotten memory: the taste of salt and wind, the memory of gusts of air that obeyed his every thought. A quiet ship on a strange river cut impossibly through hills.

DM: He pushes himself as hard as possible to catch them. But it is too late. They turn north, disappearing faster than he can catch up. No matter now. They have been still for a long time. Plenty of time. Yeah, sure he will catch them. Finally he grows closer and closer. There, in a city full of warmth of people. He swoops over the streets, enjoying the screams and shrieks of the people as his gloom stalker grabs victims and drops them from a great height and turns racing across the water towards the great stone ship where the light is.
((Battle preparations, combat mechanics and attack sequence))
DM: So with that, their shadow hunters are dispatched, and quiet returns to the waterfront of Tollen at 2 in the morning.

interactions.title: Clarifying the dwarves’ limited choices
lines: Wellby: It seems like the giants saved them from dragon, and so they agreed to some term of servitude. And it's, like, I don't know that that's exactly a fair deal, because, you know, it was negotiation at the end of the gun, but maybe.
Wellby: They're not enslaved. They didn't seem resentful about it. I don't know. Am I tracking that right, Tim?
DM: I mean. Yeah, they I would say they didn't seem resentful at all, right? I mean—
Delwath: More resigned than anything else, but they weren’t like, “Help us escape.”
Wellby: Right. Well, they were kinda like, what good does escape—
DM: More perilous places, where at the end.
Wellby: Like, their problem is that they live in this part of the world.

DM: I, I think the—I think the vibe is not so much like these are allies, but more, they feel they don't necessarily have good choices. I mean, the king is—the king is clearly not like, “Oh, my dwarven friends, I will protect you out of the goodness of my heart.”
Delwath: We didn't find this out, so I guess it's too late to find it out. But what are they mining? And why do the frost giants want mined stuff? That'd be a good question to ask.
DM: I mean, they were clearly mining iron.

before: DM: Yeah, he will be pleased to meet you. And he
DM: You know, look—glances back and see if the dwarves are all kind of standing around and watching, is like, hmm, goes stomping off on his mammoth back to the mines and sends you on your way.
Delwath: Shall we go meet this king?
Wellby: So, so sorry, just in, in summary, the dwarves—
Kenzo: What's their deal? They're, like, just kind of, like, are they in league with the giants, or are they, like, oppressed?
after: Unknown: Maybe weapons or something.
Riswynn: Build great halls.

DM: So it's a hundred miles north. It's about 90 miles north. So it's—the sun is beginning to set now, so if you leave immediately, you could get there around dawn with a short break in the middle of the night.
Delwath: I mean, unless they wanna get there in the middle of the night, which is—
DM: You could get there.
